description: A variance measures how far a list of scores spreads from its mean
code:
scores = [2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9]
spread = scores.variance()
assert(spread, 4)
scores.push(11)
spread

description: A standard deviation follows a list as readings arrive
code:
readings = [61, 58, 64]
wobble = readings.stdev()
assert(wobble, 2.449489742783178)
readings.push(57)
wobble

description: A selector measures the spread of a property over a class population
code:
class Parcel(weight):
    this.weight = weight
Parcel(3)
Parcel(5)
heavy = Parcel(10)
spread = Parcel.variance(parcel -> parcel.weight)
assert(spread, 8.666666666666666)
heavy.weight = 4
spread

description: A single value has no spread, and an empty list has NaN
code:
samples = [7]
spread = samples.variance()
assert(spread, 0)
samples.pop()
String(spread)

description: The deviations of large values keep a spread that two averages cancel
code:
ticks = [1000000001, 1000000002, 1000000003]
jitter = ticks.variance()
naive = ticks.average(t -> t * t) - ticks.average() ** 2
[jitter, naive]

description: A class-level rule keeps the standard deviation of each machine's readings
code:
class Machine(readings):
    this.readings = readings
$Machine.drift = $Machine.readings.stdev()
press = Machine([50, 54, 46])
assert(press.drift, 3.265986323710904)
press.readings.push(50)
press.drift

description: A standard deviation over a filtered population follows each new instance
code:
class Trip(city, minutes):
    this.city = city
    this.minutes = minutes
Trip("oslo", 30)
Trip("oslo", 34)
Trip("bergen", 90)
local = Trip.filter(trip -> trip.city == "oslo").stdev(trip -> trip.minutes)
assert(local, 2)
Trip("oslo", 26)
local

description: A selector that reads another variable follows it
code:
gain = 2
levels = [1, 2, 3]
spread = levels.variance(level -> level * gain)
assert(spread, 2.6666666666666665)
gain = 3
spread

description: An undefined value leaves the variance unknown until it is defined
code:
class Sensor(name):
    this.name = name
a = Sensor("a")
a.level = 4
b = Sensor("b")
spread = Sensor.variance(sensor -> sensor.level)
assert(spread, null)
b.level = 8
spread

description: A selector that is not a function raises a typed error
code:
xs = [1, 2]
failure = ""
try:
    xs.variance(2)
catch error:
    failure = error
failure

description: A failed selector rolls back the change that triggered it
code:
def checked(level):
    if level < 0:
        throw "NEGATIVE"
    return level
levels = [3, 5, 10]
spread = levels.stdev(checked)
try:
    levels.push(-1)
catch error:
    pass
[levels.length, spread]

description: Bindings and functions named variance and stdev keep their meaning
code:
variance = [1, 3]
def stdev(values) => values.length
[variance.variance(), stdev(variance), variance.stdev()]
